newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian small caps market set to see first listing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian small caps market set to see first listing.

text.p: A Belgian firm developing cancer treatment through implants aims to raise 250 million francs on the country's new small capitalisation market, EURO NM Belgium, which is waiting to see its first listing.
International Brachytherapy (IBt) is offering 250,000 shares at 1,000 Belgian francs each in a capital increase, with subscriptions to the public offer running until February 28 at the latest.
Antwerp broker Smeets, which is bringing IBt to the new Brussels market, said on Tuesday it expected the stock to be listed on the EURO NM in the first or second week of March.

The Brussels Stock Exchange said it was considering applications from five companies and could not say at this stage which would be the first to list on the new market which became technically operational last month.

The Brussels new market -- or Nouveau Marche -- project is part of a wider plan to form a federation of similar markets in Paris, Frankfurt, Amsterdam and Brussels. The Paris Nouveau Marche has already been up and running for several months.

IBt plans to develop, make and sell radiotherapeutic devices, called seeds, which can be implanted in a patient to treat prostate cancer in its early stages. The product will initially target the U.S. market.

Jean-Luc Amez from Smeets' corporate finance department said IBt would spend the money raised from the flotation on patenting, land, a factory, a cyclotron (particle accelerator to make radioisotopes) and on further development of the process.
There would also be a convertible bond issue for a further 250,000 shares within the next quarter, he added.
Smeets said in a presentation of the company that IBt's management was made up of founders and employees of Nasdaq-listed competitor Theragenics Corp.

IBt was expected to have net earnings in 1997 of minus 135 million Belgian francs, moving into the black in 1999 when net earnings were forecast at 123 million francs, climbing to 409 million by 2001.
Gross sales were projected to rise from 55 million francs in 1998 to 1.163 billion in 2001.
